name: Industry Enhancements
summary: Recipe figures, industry columns, worker status and sources, plot growth
description:
Corrects the Production card figures of industries with more than one recipe, such as the canning factory (fish or meat, each with sheet metal), shows which workers don't count for an industry's worker boost, what each worker is doing and where workers can come from, gives the statistics Industries tab columns for comparing industries and shows when raw producers next try to grow. Each feature can be turned off in the mod's Settings (the gear next to the mod when choosing a game's mods). Settings also has a Logging switch, off by default, that writes the mod's messages to the game log (stdout.txt) for bug reports.

Recipe Figures: the industry window's Production card shows one row per recipe, with each cargo's current and maximum consumption or production per year. The game shows the first recipe's figures again on later rows, so the canning factory's meat row repeats the fish figures. With this mod every row shows its own cargos' figures; a cargo two recipes share, such as sheet metal, shows the industry's total on both rows.

Worker Status: an industry's worker boost counts only workers who arrived by your lines within the last 2 years. The Boosters card shows their count and lists only them, so workers who walk, drive or haven't come by line for 2 years appear nowhere. With this mod the count adds them in brackets: 11 (8)/10 means 11 came by line, 8 more work there, and 10 are needed for the boost; the statistics window's Industries tab shows the same count in its Workplaces column. The expanded worker list shows every worker, those who don't count at 0 %, with what each is doing right now: at home, shopping or at work (green), walking, driving, waiting at a stop for a bus, tram, train, ship or aircraft (a stopwatch and the line's vehicle), or riding one, with a dot in the line's colour. Point at it for the line, the stop and where they get off; click it to open the worker's window. The next columns show where the current trip goes (click to open that building; a grey workplace for a worker who now works elsewhere), how many days the worker has been in that state (a wait over 30 days in red, since it makes people unhappy; "12 d+" means at least 12 days, as the state began before this session), the worker's happiness (the person window's face and a %, with whether it is rising or falling on hover), the distance to the worker's home town (point at it for the town, click it to open the home; sort by it to see who comes from the same town), and Time Left as a % from red (0 %) to green (100 %). The worker's name moves into the location button's tooltip. The list starts with the workers on their way to work here, the longest under way first, and every column can be sorted. Perk windows show their workers the same way.

Worker Sources: the worker boost needs workers who come by your lines, but the industry window doesn't show which towns they could come from; the game draws arrows from nearby towns only for a worker subsidy. With this mod, expanding an industry's Boosters card draws arrows from the 5 closest towns (the towns a worker subsidy shows) and from any town that sends workers now. An arrow moves only while its town sends workers; a still, white arrow is a town that could. A booster cargo, such as tools, is an input, so its suppliers are in the Input Stocks card.

Statistics - Column Enhancements: the statistics window's Industries tab gets columns for comparing industries: Name, Problems, Plots, Recipe In, Recipe Out, Workload, Input, Output, Shipment, Boosters and Workplaces. Plots shows a raw producer's plots built of the most it may have (5/8), so you can find the ones that can grow largest. Recipe In and Recipe Out show each recipe's input and output cargos a year without boosts, a line per recipe in the same order as Input and Output, and sort by the largest. Workload adds what the boosts on now add in green, so Input is about Recipe In × Workload × (1 + boost). Input, Output and Shipment show an icon and amount per cargo and sort by the sum; each Shipment amount is coloured by its share of what the industry made of that cargo in the last year (green from 67%, yellow from 33%, red below), with the share on hover. Boosters shows how much faster each cargo booster makes production, in green while it is on. Workplaces adds the worker boost the same way after the worker count. Both sort the boosts that are on first, then by how much they add. Requirements is left out, since Input shows the same cargos.

Plot Growth: a raw producer (mine, farm, forest, well…) grows by one plot at a time, which raises its output. The game tries every half year, with a chance from how well it produces and how much of its output your lines ship: none at 25 % or less, sure from 75 %. The industry window's Production card doesn't say any of this. With this mod the row under the plots icon shows the plots built of the most the industry may have (15/20) and when the next try comes (43 days): green when it will succeed, yellow when it may, grey when it can't, also while the industry is blocked from further expansion (the try adds no plot unless the way is clear by then). Hover it for the chance and what it is made of. The statistics window's Plots column (Industry Columns) shows the same.

params.name: Recipe Figures
params.tooltip: In an industry's Production card, every recipe row shows its own cargos' figures (the game repeats the first recipe's); a cargo two recipes share shows its total.

params.name: Plot Growth
params.tooltip: The industry window's Production card shows under a raw producer's plots the most it may have and when the game next tries to add a plot (green sure, yellow maybe, grey no chance or blocked from further expansion).

params.name: Worker Status
params.tooltip: The Boosters card counts every worker, also those who don't count for the worker boost (they walk, drive or haven't come by line in 2 years), as does the statistics Industries tab's Workplaces column. Its worker list shows them all with what each does now (at home, shopping, at work, walking, driving, waiting for or riding a bus, tram, train, ship or aircraft, with the line on hover), where the trip goes, for how many days, the worker's happiness, how far their home town is, and Time Left as a coloured %; the name moves into a tooltip.

params.name: Worker Sources
params.tooltip: Expanding an industry's Boosters card shows arrows from the towns its workers can come from: the closest towns and any town that sends workers now. An arrow moves while its town sends workers.

params.name: Statistics - Column Enhancements
params.tooltip: The statistics Industries tab shows plots, each input and output a year without boosts (Recipe In / Out), the boosts on now beside Workload, input, output and shipment per cargo (shipment coloured by the share of last year's production shipped), and each booster's and the worker boost's production increase (green while on); Requirements is left out.

params.name: Logging
params.tooltip: Writes the mod's messages to the game log (stdout.txt), for bug reports.
